First of all, I don't understand why people call this fake, scam and things like that. 

Nothing he said is a tall claim, he worked in IT for 20+ years without any exposure to stock investment or trading, he  saved from his salary to invest in the market that too only after formally learning how stocks and derivatives work by doing a course in a reputed institution (IIM Calcutta). He learnt the basics before coming to the markets and still had ups/downs for years. He is not shying away from admitting that its a struggle. Also, he is not trying to attract new comers to option trading rightaway, he is clearly saying if someone has minimum capital and no knowledge, he should not come to trading and instead invest in mutual funds etc. That itself is a proof of his honesty. 

I attended his course in Bangalore in Aug this year. Was amazed with the depth of knowledge, both in stock market and the tool development using AI. I haven't heard any bad feedback from anyone who attended that training. Everyone felt that it was a very useful course. That doesn't mean we all understood everything he taught, there were concepts he didn't explain the basics and went straight into building tools. Thats because many participants of the course had experience trading options already and were clear on the concepts. 

Only recommendation I have for his team is that they should clearly list some pre-requisites to attend his course, like good knowledge on options. They should also give video/document that participants can go thru and learn the basics before coming to the course. While they had onboarding sessions for people who had no coding experience, they didn't provide anything to people with no/little knowledge on derivatives. May be its because they thought everyone who wants to learn advanced option trading had experience (good/bad) with option trading already. 

So, in short if you know the basics of option trading already and had experience with trading (either successful or not) you can definitely learn a lot from him. I will definitely attend his course again if he announces a new one. Thats because after attending the course in Aug, I started trading options regularly and I feel I am better prepared to understand his teaching now. That doesn't mean I am using the techniques he taught, Im not, I am still working on the developing a model based on his teaching which I can use to trade in future. But, if a person who knew basics attended his course, he would have started practicing it the next day. 

I am very confident that he is not like many influencers on YouTube who talk as if they can predict every market movement and keep throwing random tips everyday and forgets what he spoke the previous day. He is a person who achieved financial freedom practicing what is he is preaching and all who want to travel in the same path should respect and follow him. 

I am just a student of his, not part of his team/business. I thought I should share my candid feedback since I had firsthand experience with his expertise and teaching. Thats all. You should take your own call to listen to him/ join his course based on your path/goals/plans in life. All the very best.!

Reality Check: Derivatives Are Active Work, Not "Passive" Income 
Online videos often describe option selling as "effortless passive income." This is technically misleading. 
 
The Flaw in the "Passive" Label: Selling Covered Calls and Cash-Secured Puts requires active delta monitoring, position management, roll-overs. And assignment risk management. If a stock falls 30%, a Covered Call only cushions 2% to 3% of the drop. If a stock rallies 40%, a Covered Call caps your upside. 
The Real Requirement: Ravindra spends six hours a day (9:00 AM to 3:40 PM) in his home office tracking market data and coding analytical algorithms. He also spent six months studying derivatives before placing his first order. 
The Grounded Truth: Do not attempt systematic option selling expecting a hands-off paycheck. It is an active quantitative skill that requires capital, discipline, and emotional detachment.
